title: Lua coroutine consumer subsystem findings
scope: Identify which client subsystem(s) actually use the BCS-Y-0477/0478 Lua coroutine wrappers (lua_resume / lua_yield). Follow-on to the 6A/6C verification pass that proved the coroutine API surface exists in the binary.

namedCallers.evidence: Body calls FUN_00447260("Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaThreadImpl::Resume", DAT_00f67298) as a diagnostic string before the lua_resume callsite.
namedCallers.behavior: Iterates an argument vector at param_1+0x100..+0x104 pushing each entry to the Lua stack via FUN_00cf9630, then invokes FUN_00CF4230(argCount, &errSlot). Public Resume entry of the Component::Lua::GameEngine::LuaThreadImpl C++ class.

namedCallers.name: LuaNApi__luaGameEngineRequire_FUN_00D08A10
namedCallers.evidence: Body contains two literal strings registered by FUN_00447260: `_luaGameEngineRequire` (the N-API name) at the request-side path and `_luaGameEngineRequireYield` (the yield marker) at the yield-branch path. Body calls FUN_00D0CFB0 to drive the require pipeline, branches on its return value, and yields via FUN_00CF38D0 when the result indicates async wait.
namedCallers.behavior: Lua N-API implementation of `_luaGameEngineRequire`. When the require loader (FUN_00D0CFB0) reports the script is not yet loaded, the calling Lua thread is yielded with marker `_luaGameEngineRequireYield`; the thread is later resumed by the async completion path. Returns 0/1/2 depending on completion state.
namedCallers.callersBasis: No static callers were recovered. This is consistent with Lua N-API bindings being invoked through a function table (LuaState user functions are registered via FUN_00CCCAD0 and called by the Lua VM rather than by static C calls).

Pairs with BCS-Y-0480 _luaGameEngineRequire yield path.

model.summary: The principal client use of Lua coroutines in 1.23b is asynchronous module loading. When a Lua script calls `_luaGameEngineRequire(path)`, the native impl (BCS-Y-0480 FUN_00D08A10) drives the LPB loader (BCS-Y-0466 LuaLpbLoaderResourceEvent_FUN_00D0FD70 pipeline). If the requested resource is not yet loaded, the Lua thread yields with the diagnostic marker `_luaGameEngineRequireYield`. When the loader's resource event later completes, the async completion path (BCS-Y-0481 FUN_00D0C070) prepares the require result on the stack and calls lua_resume to continue the suspended script. This pairs cleanly with the finding that `.prog` chunks load through an asynchronous LPB resource event.
model.secondaryUses: The l2 pass identifies FUN_00CCFFE0 as BCS-Y-0482, a generic LuaThreadImpl call-or-resume helper rather than a subsystem-specific coroutine consumer. FUN_00CCEAC0 and FUN_00D04DA0 remain unpromoted after the mandated one-round halt: their l2 callers are thin wrappers with no diagnostic or N-API binding strings.
model.confirmedNegativeRetained: This remains correct: the deferred event-condition execution path (FUN_00897310, FUN_008955C0) does NOT use Lua coroutines. The coroutine surface and the deferred event surface are independent.
